result.report:
PASS for the stated product criterion and bounded real-PA obstacle package. I reconstructed the embedded n100 proof rather than relying on its receipt, origin, or hash. The original arbitrary-balanced-pair classification remains open.

Lemmas 1–2 establish the finite-generation, closedness, projection, and support-alternative statements used subsequently. Homogenization preserves pointedness, Fourier–Motzkin elimination preserves rational data, and the nearest-point separation argument gives the required support form with the correct sign. Thus n100’s finite-generation dependency is also supplied within the combined argument.

Lemma 3 correctly characterizes actual PCC convexity on a fixed finite rational complex. Necessity uses rational endpoints but permits arbitrary real barycentric coefficients. Sufficiency first establishes local support, then convexity along every carrier segment, and finally the PCC inequality on any admissible structure. It does not assume global ambient extendibility. Lemma 4 consequently tests every nonnegative real local balanced cycle, including lower-dimensional cycles on ordinary open sets.

Lemma 5 gives an exact decomposition. The lifted feasibility system is rational; retaining precisely the active inequalities defines a rational subspace. A sufficiently small rational coordinate box preserves all remaining inequalities and strict recession-slope conditions. Its positive barycentric weights reproduce the original real coefficients exactly. Pointedness and the finite recession-generator tests are established, including the bounded-cell and zero-dimensional cases.

The divisor reconstruction preserves saturated quotient lattices. The two-dimensional calculation retains the plane indices χ_rs and the tangential correction −Σ_r t_r a(u_r)b(u_r); the resulting second-divisor expression is symmetric. Refinement cancellation, ambient-affine invariance, locality, and the direct-lattice product rule justify every subsequent intersection. The fixed rational coefficient spaces also justify n100’s extension of polynomial identities to real coefficients and weights. The underlying [Allermann–Rau proof](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0709.3705v3#page=9) was checked: its abbreviated commutativity display omits that symmetric tangential term, whereas the supplied reconstruction includes it and independently proves the conclusion.

The trap calculation includes all interior diagonals and factor axes. Clearing the rational maps’ denominators does not assume that the rays collectively generate a saturated lattice. The primitive diagonal h_ij, quotient covector, and bend coefficient 2g_ijα_iβ_j are correct. The first divisor is balanced, A²=B²=0, and B·A=4CC′δ₀. The direct product expansion has exactly the exponent vector (2,1,…,1), with multiplicity d!/2!, giving the complete coefficient κ=2^(m+2)d!CC′e∏M_l. The balanced zero curve supplies the claimed actual PCC.

The real-reference gluing is valid. Each rational component has the common coercive lower bound, and each component maximum has rational comparison walls. Their weighted sum introduces no new walls. It equals λQ on ρ≤2R and γ−M̄ on ρ≥S, so the prescribed exterior reference is restored exactly. Lemma 4 establishes PAPC, and P+1/j establishes the regularizable domain directly.

The envelope proof bounds every raw competitor at zero, then at rational points by radial PCCs, and finally at real points by rational simplices with real coefficients. It uses no continuity assumption on competitors. P itself satisfies the envelope’s obstacle and growth bounds. Therefore Pγ(u)=P globally. Recursive locality gives λ^dκδ₀ inside the roof ball; the integrand vanishes everywhere else, including its boundary. Hence the complete defect is −ελ^dκ. The mixed rectangle difference and the choice ε∈{1,2} guarantee nonseparability.

The positive proof in n100 also closes. Its rational Jensen splitting establishes ambient convex majorants for raw competitors. The finite epigraph construction gives the actual envelope and bounded reference difference. Projected lower graph faces have rational spatial generators even when their heights are real, so the required rational domains follow. At a noncontact potential atom, the selected generators produce a nonzero rational subspace L annihilated by active slope differences. Every application of the vanishing statements supplies an everywhere-defined quotient function and rational quotient fan. The three cases establish, respectively, quotient dimension at most m<d, quotient dimension at most d−1 inside one cell, or common nonzero affine lineality. Thus branching-face contributions are covered and all noncontact atoms vanish. Bivalent factors, complete affine space, and the point case are handled correctly.

The embedded tripod example, n100’s rational-reference construction, and the irrational-reference illustration agree with these calculations; the latter has defect −1/2 and mixed difference 1/2+2θ.

Source conventions were checked against the [versioned BMPS PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). Harmless wording clarification: references to “real regularizability” describe the draft’s explicitly defined real analogue, rather than a real-slope theorem imported from BMPS. Every measured envelope here is already PAPC with explicit constant-shift approximants. No substantial repair, whole-pair regularity assumption, analytic realization, or broader classification is needed.
